clue.text: Region much fresher as broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the clue word is taken by its sound

parts.note: much fresher air is airier, and in a non-rhotic accent that word is said like a word for a region

explanation.surface: A district whose air seems far cleaner, as a weather bulletin might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as broadcast' signals a sound-alike: AIRIER, said in a British accent with no final R, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A region and an area are synonyms for a stretch of land or a zone.

clue.text: Dispute is only half on an equal basis

indicators.note: only half of the little word is kept, here its second letter

parts.note: on a par means equal, so par stands for an equal footing

explanation.surface: An argument that only half deserves to be treated as balanced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' keeps just S, the back half of 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to argue or wrangle, a verb sense of exchanging blows in words.

clue.text: An artist on the lathe?

definitions.meaning: J. M. W. ... was the great English painter of light and sea
a craftsman who shapes wood or metal on a lathe is one who turns it

explanation.surface: Picturing a painter working at a woodworking machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The painter Turner shares his surname with the trade name for a lathe operator.

clue.text: Fatty requires active duty shortly, I suggest

parts.note: A is the grammar abbreviation for active

indicators.note: shortly cuts the word down to its opening letter

parts.note: to pose a question or idea is to suggest it

explanation.surface: A slimmer is told a short stint of exercise is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose is the technical adjective for tissue made of or storing fat.

clue.text: Alienate sergeant, terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of the word are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Advice, or a warning, about upsetting a sergeant badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' reads as an adverb on 'Alienate' but scrambles SERGEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to alienate them, making them unfriendly or distant.

clue.text: Film musical found a way to come back with old title restored

indicators.note: coming back means the letters run in the reverse direction

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

indicators.note: restored means the letters are reworked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A screen musical found a route back to its original name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come back' turns RD into DR; 'restored' rearranges OLD TITLE into DOLITTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Dolittle (1967) is a Hollywood musical film about a vet who talks to animals.

clue.text: Party endorses transfers

parts.note: CON is short for the Conservative Party
to sign a document is to endorse it

explanation.surface: A political party approves the movement of members or players.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign goods is to hand them over or send them, a synonym for transfer.

clue.text: Put forward case in favour of keeping sterling

indicators.note: keeping here means holding alongside, placing one piece next to the other

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, meaning in favour of
the pound is the unit of sterling, Britain's currency

explanation.surface: A financial argument for retaining the pound rather than adopting the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: To propound is to offer an argument or theory for consideration.

clue.text: Basis for wholesaling line creates grief

parts.note: SOR stands for sale or return, the terms on which goods are often supplied in bulk
a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A trade arrangement that ends in heartache.
explanation.walkthrough: Sale or return lets a retailer send back unsold stock; it is abbreviated SOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrow and grief are synonyms for deep sadness.

clue.text: Paying customer to make severe criticism about rotten first half performance

indicators.note: about means the criticism word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: a performance, a fuss or carry-on, signals that the letters are reworked
the first half of the word is all that is kept

explanation.surface: A critic slates a dreadful first half of a show, watched by a paying customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance' here is a fuss or song and dance, so it rearranges the half-word it follows; 'about' wraps the criticism word around the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a regular client or customer of a shop, restaurant or theatre.

clue.text: Historically imprisoned one of many on Dartmoor

indicators.note: imprisoned means the letters are locked up inside the clue word

explanation.surface: A Dartmoor prison inmate of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Dartmoor is a moorland in Devon, England, famous for its prison and its rocky hilltops.
explanation.definitionFit: Dartmoor is dotted with tors, granite outcrops crowning its hills.

clue.text: Sociable swimmer expressed sympathy for sick cat

indicators.note: expressed means spoken, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: poor puss is what one says to comfort an ailing cat

explanation.surface: Someone said kind words to an ailing pet cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Porpoises are marine mammals that swim in social groups called pods.

clue.text: Even let go of one's own identity

indicators.note: even means the letters in even positions, second, fourth and sixth, are taken

explanation.surface: Even surrendering one's sense of self.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adverb but picks the even-placed letters of 'let go of'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is the self, a person's sense of their own identity.

clue.text: Newspaper copy

definitions.meaning: the Daily ... is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: The Mirror is a UK tabloid, and to mirror is to imitate or reproduce.

clue.text: Overmodest up north at the end of the last century

definitions.meaning: a dialect word of northern England and Scotland for prim or demure

definitions.text: at the end of the last century
definitions.meaning: M plus IM, a loose Roman numeral for 1999, the last year of the twentieth century

explanation.walkthrough: Strictly 1999 is MCMXCIX, but MIM (1000 + 999) is a well-known shortcut.
explanation.definitionFit: Mim is a northern dialect word for prim, and MIM is an informal Roman numeral for 1999.

clue.text: Thought once again about beasts getting distressed ending

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
asses are beasts of burden
the closing three letters of the word distressed

explanation.surface: Animals in distress make someone reconsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes the last three letters, SED, of 'distressed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess something is to consider or evaluate it once more.

clue.text: Agonised about site of US naval base

indicators.note: about here means the letters are turned around and moved about

explanation.surface: Worrying over a Californian navy port.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego in California hosts the largest US Navy base on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Maverick Guatemalan let out of nearby capital

indicators.note: maverick means unruly and wayward, so the letters run wild
out of means the letters of the short word are taken away from the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: A rebellious Guatemalan is released from a neighbouring city.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange GUATEMALAN with L, E, T removed: GUAMAAN gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Managua is the capital of Nicaragua, a near neighbour of Guatemala in Central America.

clue.text: One who gets off with a detective chief superintendent?

parts.note: CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department of detectives
a chief or superintendent is a head

explanation.surface: A senior police officer sleeps with someone, or catches them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets off' is slang for getting high, not for escaping a charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid head is slang for a regular user of LSD, someone who gets high.

clue.text: Like P, T, K and S, conducive to change without a leader

definitions.text: Like P, T, K and S

indicators.note: to change means the letters must be altered into a new order
without a leader means the first letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Something said to encourage change once a leader is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a leader' drops the C of CONDUCIVE; 'to change' rearranges ONDUCIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetics calls consonants like p, t, k and s voiceless, produced without vibrating the vocal cords.

clue.text: Fed up with exam for the most skilful

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: a test is an exam

explanation.surface: Fed up with the exam set for the top students.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft means nimble and skilled, so its superlative is the most skilful.

clue.text: Article penned by another

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed within, the letters held inside the word

explanation.surface: A piece of writing by a different author.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' is the definite article.

clue.text: Bring matter to court about tabloid newspaper slight

indicators.note: about means the filing word wraps around the newspaper word

parts.note: to file a suit is to bring a case before a court
a rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: Taking a tabloid to court over a small insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slight' looks like a noun meaning a snub, but it is the adjective meaning delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight and fragile both describe something frail and easily broken.

clue.text: Dish is served, cut into pieces

indicators.note: to dish something is to ruin it, so the letters are wrecked and reordered

explanation.surface: A plate of food is served, already sliced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' looks like the food but is the verb meaning spoil, scrambling IS SERVED.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissever is to sever or divide into parts, so cut into pieces fits as a past participle.

clue.text: Anxious concerning the border

parts.note: on means about or concerning, as in a talk on art
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: Worried about the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge is an idiom for being nervous or tense.

clue.text: Central European solicitor not to participate

indicators.note: central means the middle letters of the word are taken

parts.note: a tout solicits custom, so is one who solicits

explanation.surface: A lawyer from mainland Europe declining a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but means a tout touting for business.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt out is to choose not to take part.

clue.text: Old Indian postal system had beginnings in Delhi and Karachi

indicators.note: the beginnings, the first letters, of the next words are taken

explanation.surface: A former subcontinental post service started out in two big cities.
explanation.definitionFit: The dak was the relay mail and transport service of British India.

clue.text: This queen applied for release, as originally predicted

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A queen sought freedom, just as foretold.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen is Cleopatra, who freed herself from capture by applying a venomous snake to her body.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra is said to have killed herself with the bite of an Egyptian cobra.

clue.text: Reported trying to catch a computer scam

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: angling for fish is trying to catch them

explanation.surface: News of an attempt to catch out an online fraudster.
explanation.definitionFit: Phishing is fraudulent email or messaging that lures people into revealing passwords or bank details.

clue.text: Defrauded over relationship

parts.note: too means excessively, as in overdone
kin is family, people related by blood

explanation.surface: Cheated in a romance or over a family tie.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken in is to be deceived or swindled, an idiom for being conned.

clue.text: Forewarning of submarine captain being sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the letters go in reverse order

parts.note: Captain Nemo commands the Nautilus in Jules Verne's novels

explanation.surface: A warning of a submarine commander being recalled.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign of what is to come, a portent or warning.

clue.text: Scrap part of audiotape

indicators.note: part of means a portion of the word's letters is taken

explanation.surface: Discard a section of recording tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a verb, discard, but is a noun meaning a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota, from the smallest Greek letter, is a tiny bit or jot.

clue.text: Flower arrangement for relaxed cream tea? No thanks!

indicators.note: relaxed means loosened up, so the letters are moved around
no means the letters of the thanks word are taken out of the pool

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks

explanation.surface: An informal afternoon tea is politely declined.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T and A from CREAM TEA and rearrange CREAME. A cream tea is a British treat of tea with scones, jam and clotted cream.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a raceme is a flower cluster arranged along a central stem, like a foxglove.

clue.text: Honour vehicle crew verbally

indicators.note: verbally means spoken out, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: a lorry is a goods vehicle and an eight is a rowing crew

explanation.surface: Praise for the team driving a vehicle, spoken out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: A lorry is a British truck; an eight is a rowing boat's crew of eight oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: To laureate someone is to crown them with laurel, an old sign of distinction.
